chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, that Al-Hakam asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

about a man who was gifted a dove inside the Al-Haram, clipped (of feathers). So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Take it and be good to it, and feed it until when its feathers are complete (grown back), so free its way'.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specific holy sanctuary, often referring to Mecca or the Prophet's mosque
key_terms.فَخَلِّ سَبِيلَهَا: So free its way / Release it
key_terms.مَقْصُوصَةٌ: Clipped (referring to a bird whose flight feathers have been cut)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a clipped dove gifted inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) illustrates the principle of *ihsan* (excellence) in animal care, specifically addressing the status of birds within the sacred precincts of Mecca. It establishes a practical protocol for temporary captivity and rehabilitation of clipped birds, distinguishing between the prohibition of hunting in the Haram and the permissibility of caring for gifted birds until they are fully restored for release.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara that, 
‘Al-Hakam asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

about a man who was gifted a clipped dove inside the Al-Harram. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Take it and be good to it, and look after it until when its feathers are complete (grown back), so free its way’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa form Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Al-Hakam once asked abu Ja’far ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who receives a pigeon as a gift in al- Haram (the sacred area) with its wings shortened. He (the Imam) said, ‘He takes it, looks after it and feeds it until its wings grow, then sets it free.’”
